result.title: Understanding Personalization Gains in Whisper
result.summary: Whisper-style ASR models provide strong zero-shot transcription, but their residual errors are not evenly distributed across datasets, recording conditions, and metadata-based groups. We study when lightweight low-rank adaptation (LoRA) improves Whisper and whether observed gains require group-specific adapters. Across Common Voice, LibriSpeech, and VoxPopuli, we compare zero-shot Whisper, pooled LoRA, and group-specific LoRA under matched within-group splits. We find that adaptation is not uniformly beneficial: gains are concentrated in difficult Common Voice groups, are consistent on VoxPopuli, and largely disappear on low-error LibriSpeech. Crucially, pooled LoRA often matches, and sometimes clearly outperforms, group-specific LoRA. Gains over zero-shot should therefore be tested against matched pooled adaptation before being interpreted as evidence of personalization.

AI.brief_summary: 研究 Whisper 类语音识别模型经 LoRA 微调后的组间增益来源，发现增益集中于困难群体，且共享（pooled）适配器常可与群体专属适配器持平甚至更优。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作属语音识别领域的适配器微调与个性化效果分析，不涉及视觉或多模态推理状态、latent 生成、证据获取与停止决策，也未提出可用于 LVR 的方法线索，故排除。
